q: Terras's theorem on the Collatz stopping time σ(n) (first time the orbit drops below n) states that for almost all n:
opts: σ(n) is always infinite (the orbit never drops)
exp: Terras (1976): σ(n) ~ log(n)/log(4/3) for density-1 set of n. Each step of the Collatz map multiplies by 3/4 on average (half the time ÷2, half the time ×3/2), so it takes ≈log(n)/|log(3/4)| = log(n)/log(4/3) steps to drop below n.
